title: Dominic and the Ember
premise: Freya Reyes keeps the ledgers of the Ember, a guild that trades in impossible things—stolen years, bottled grief, memories pried from sleeping minds. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Freya learns the boy is a soul sold to the court beneath the mountain, and that the guild's own ledgers record the sale. To save him, Freya must steal back what was lawfully purchased before the moon completes its thirteenth turn, betraying the found family that made him and unmasking the guildmaster who has been feeding souls to the deep court for decades. In the end Freya burns the ledgers, shatters the guild's power, and chooses justice outside the law—raising the child not as property or payment, but as kin.
about_author: Rosalind Okafor is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a coastal city's records office before turning to fiction full-time. She writes about thieves, ledgers, and the quiet violence of institutions from a house full of rescued cats and unreliable clocks.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Things
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A night of routine thefts introduces the Ember guild: its rules, its ledger-room, its code of invisibility. Freya catalogs a stolen memory and feels nothing, which frightens him. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Thirteenth Hour
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A child appears at the guild's hidden door, barefoot in snow, speaking a language no one knows—except the ledger itself seems to recognize it. The guild debates turning him out. Emotional beat: Freya's first crack of empathy in years.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Examining old ledgers, Freya finds an entry matching the child's strange sigils: 'one soul, sold, payable beneath the mountain.' Guildmaster Corvane dismisses it as clerical error. Emotional beat: dread taking root.

chapters.title: The Language of Before
chapters.summary: Child's POV (rendered through Freya's translation attempts). Flashback fragments reveal the boy's village traded their children's souls for a winter that never ended. Emotional beat: innocence carrying unbearable history.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The child, named Ash by the cook Maren, settles into guild life; small found-family moments—shared meals, mended boots. But Corvane watches Ash too closely. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Moon Owes
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. An old midwife explains the moon-count: thirteen turns until the debt comes due, when the mountain court will collect Ash bodily. Emotional beat: a ticking clock made flesh.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room at Night
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya breaks his own rule and steals from the guild—copying pages proving Corvane has sold dozens of souls over thirty years. Emotional beat: betrayal of the only home he's known.

chapters.title: Buyers and Sellers
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya traces a buyer's mark to Lady Vess, a noble whose son's soul was bought back at ruinous price—the only rescue on record. Emotional beat: hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Nightmares show the mountain court: gilded, patient, hungry. Ash begins speaking Freya's language, and his first word is 'ledger.' Emotional beat: the past reaching forward.

chapters.title: An Offer, Politely Made
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane offers Freya partnership—and reveals he knows about the copied pages. He frames the soul-trade as mercy: the court must be fed or it rises. Emotional beat: corruption wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: Thieves' Parliament
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya secretly meets rival thieves and Vess; they form a fragile conspiracy to breach the mountain. Trust is currency none of them can afford. Emotional beat: alliance built on mutual blackmail.

chapters.title: The Turn of the Tenth Moon
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The guild fractures; some members side with Corvane. Maren hides Ash in the memory-vaults, where stored lives whisper around him. Emotional beat: family choosing sides.

chapters.title: What Freya Stole First
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Flashback chapter: young Freya sold his own childhood memories to the Ember to escape his father's debts—he cannot remember why he once wept. Emotional beat: understanding the true cost of the trade.

chapters.title: The Descent Road
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The conspiracy enters the mountain's throat through an abandoned mine, guided by Vess's bought-back knowledge. Betrayal within the group costs them their guide. Emotional beat: fear sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: Gilding and Rot
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The deep court revealed: beautiful, bureaucratic, endlessly polite. Souls are filed like assets. Vess bargains for passage using her son's story as leverage. Emotional beat: horror administered with courtesy.

chapters.title: The Reading of Accounts
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya stands before the court's auditor and argues the sale was fraudulent—Corvane sold what he never owned. The court agrees to hear evidence. Emotional beat: a thief finding justice in the enemy's own system.

chapters.title: Corvane Descends
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Cornered, Corvane arrives to buy his way out, offering Freya's erased memories as payment for Ash's soul. Emotional beat: temptation aimed precisely at the wound.

chapters.title: The Price of Remembering
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Climax part one: Freya refuses the offer, presents the forged-and-true ledgers, and Corvane's crimes are read aloud. The court voids the sale—but demands a keeper's bond: someone must hold Ash's soul in trust. Emotional beat: victory with strings attached.

chapters.title: What Burns
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Climax part two: escaping the collapsing court as the moon completes its turn, Freya realizes the guild will simply sell again. He burns the master ledgers in the vaults above, erasing every claim. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into liberation.

chapters.title: After the Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The guild scatters; Corvane, stripped of his records, is delivered to the thieves' parliament for judgment outside any lawful court. Maren takes stock of who remains. Emotional beat: exhausted relief.

chapters.title: Kin
chapters.summary: Freya and Ash shared POV. Freya signs himself as Ash's keeper in a new, honest book—one page, two names. Ash teaches him one word of the old language: it means 'home.' Emotional beat: found family made deliberate.

chapters.title: The Ember and the Ash
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, coda. A year later, Freya runs no guild—only a safehouse where stolen things are returned to their owners. A new knock comes at the door. Emotional beat: the work of justice never ends, but no one carries it alone.
